{{Short description|Czech mathematician (1925–1999)}}
'''Vlastimil Pták''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈvlascɪmɪl ˈptaːk}}; 8 November 1925 in [[Prague]] – 5 May <!--one source says 9 May--> 1999) was a [[Czechs|Czech]] [[mathematician]]. He worked in [[functional analysis]], theoretical [[numerical analysis]], and [[linear algebra]]. Notable early work include generalizations of the [[open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]].<ref>See ''Completeness and the open mapping theorem'' (an English-language summary of his work in this area), in {{slink||Selected publications}}, and its reviews by [[Victor Klee]] ({{MR|0105606}}) and [[Ákos Császár]] ({{zbl|0082.32502}}, in German)</ref>

During 1945–1949, Vlastimil Pták studied mathematics and physics at the [[Charles University]] in Prague. Later, he worked at the university and since 1952 in Mathematical Institute of [[Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences]]. In 1965 he was named professor at the Charles University. He has published more than 160 mathematical research papers. He had three Ph.D. students: [[Nicholas Young (mathematician)| Nicholas Young]], Michal Zajac and Miroslav Engliš. <ref>{{mathgenealogy|154039}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*''Completeness and the open mapping theorem.'' Bull. Soc. Math. France 86 1958 41–74. [http://www.numdam.org/numdam-bin/item?id=BSMF_1958__86__41_0 Text online]
*''On complete topological linear spaces.'' Czechoslovak Math. J. 3(78), (1953). 301–364.
*''On matrices with non-positive off-diagonal elements and positive principal minors.'' (with Miroslav Fiedler) Czechoslovak Math. J. 12 (87) 1962 382–400.
